admission.justification: OR-R035's recorded worklist basis carries the real alternatives it decided: leaving the size unnamed, the pre-ruling state the packet's Problem describes, and requiring fan-out at every size, against a threshold drawn from the actual worklists.

alternatives.option: One deduplicated full-intake list of distinct outstanding memory actions; at 100 or more actionable entries fan out read/search/reference checks one level where the harness supports it, below 100 it is optional, and an unsupported harness works alone and reports the limit; every durable write, semantic judgment, full memory-quality run and the handoff stay with the main Curator.
alternatives.reason: The large passes gain bounded read help without moving any judgment or write, and short passes stay solo.

alternatives.option: Leave the size unnamed and let the Curator judge when to use the helpers.
alternatives.reason: That was the pre-ruling state: the packet's Problem records that no sentence told the Curator when to use them, so a large worklist could be read alone.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The role texts surface a large worklist to the Curator by another means.

alternatives.option: Require the helpers for every pass regardless of size.
alternatives.reason: The master's own worklists include small passes (49=14, 70=40, 76=71, 75=88) where the solo path is complete; OR-R035 allows fan-out below 100 and requires it at 100 or more.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Real passes below the threshold show hidden read-heavy work that the solo path misses.

consequences: The Curator role text names the deduplicated list, the 100 threshold, what is handed out and what stays with the main session.
This very pass reports its own list size and its harness support against that rule.
context: The Curator role already allowed one-level read/search/reference sub-agents but named no size at which to use them.
